title: Policy evaluation: allow, explicit deny and permission boundaries

videos.script: When a request reaches AWS, something has to decide yes or no. This lesson is that decision. {{start}} Every request starts as a no. Nobody has to write that down. {{deny}} Then AWS looks for an explicit deny, in any policy at all. If it finds one, the answer is no, whatever else allows it. {{layers}} After that come two kinds of layer. Some can only take permissions away: the organisation's guardrails, a permission boundary, a session policy. The others grant: the identity's own policies, and the resource's. A request has to pass every limit, and find at least one grant. {{moto}} moto checks some of this, and not all of it. You will watch it refuse and allow exactly as AWS would. You will also watch it ignore a boundary, a bucket policy and a condition. Each time, the lesson says what AWS would have done instead. {{tools}} And it names the tools that check against AWS itself, for the day the lab is not enough. {{end}}
